sources.title: Glenn Flierl and Raffaele Ferrari, MIT OpenCourseWare 12.820, Turbulence in the Ocean and Atmosphere, Chapter 3 (Spring 2006 lecture notes)
sources.locator: Complete 11-page Chapter 3 PDF, §§3.1–3.8; especially §3.3 (statistical symmetries), §3.6 (closure problem), §3.7 (Reynolds equations), and §3.8 (eddy-viscosity closure).

contents.name: §3.1 Probability density functions and moments
contents.reason: The assigned A item defines fixed finite weights and asserts no probability-density, moment-integrability, or sampled-data result.

contents.name: §3.2 Joint probability density functions and covariance
contents.support: The source's statistical covariance is used only to contextualize the finite algebraic covariance; the item states the exact finite weighted definition and does not import a probability-space definition.

contents.name: §3.3 Ergodicity and statistical symmetries
contents.support: The section distinguishes ensemble, time, and spatial averaging and makes equivalence depend on assumptions; the remark asserts none of those equivalences.

contents.name: §3.4 Central Limit Theorem
contents.reason: No large-sample limit or statistical inference is claimed.

contents.name: §3.5 Intermittency
contents.reason: No probability-density shape, intermittency measure, or empirical turbulence classification is claimed.

contents.name: §3.6 The Closure Problem
contents.support: The source explains that nonlinear averaging leaves covariance information and that closure requires added assumptions; the remark records this as modeling context and asserts no universal closure theorem.

contents.name: §3.7 The Reynolds equations
contents.support: The source presents a statistical mean momentum equation with an eddy covariance term; the local mathematical supplier proves the stated finite fixed-weight identity without statistical-limit assumptions.

contents.name: §3.8 Eddy viscosity and eddy diffusivity
contents.reason: No eddy-viscosity or eddy-diffusivity closure formula is adopted or proved.

sources.title: H. Tennekes and J. L. Lumley, A First Course in Turbulence (1972), full-text digital copy
sources.locator: Complete book text; Preface pp. xi–xii and Chapter 2 §2.1, printed pp. 27–33. The complete rendered §2.1 was inspected for time-average assumptions, Reynolds decomposition, the stress sign, and the unclosed moment hierarchy.

contents.name: Preface, pp. xi–xii
contents.support: The authors describe closure as additional modeling/estimation work; this supports the remark's warning that the exact identity does not select a closure.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §2.1, printed pp. 27–33
contents.support: The section defines a long-time mean under a statistically steady condition and explains how covariance enters the mean equation and produces a hierarchy; the remark does not import those averaging hypotheses.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §2.1, printed pp. 27–33, mean stress convention
contents.support: The book writes the fluctuation stress with a negative covariance sign in the mean stress. The example derives its own signed correction directly from the finite supplier equation and the declared plus-divergence convention.
